origin: From the fairy tale Hansel and Gretel, where the siblings drop breadcrumbs so they won't get lost. It means you can retrace the path you came by.
whenToUse: The hierarchy has three or more levels, such as categories or folders.
People often land on deep pages straight from search or outside links.
People often need to go back up to a parent list.
whenNotToUse: The site is simple, with only one or two levels.
You're showing progress through steps, such as checkout.
You'd use it in place of browser history (Back).

alternatives.name: Tabs
alternatives.reason: Moving between screens at the same level.

accessibility: Make a landmark with <nav aria-label> and express the path as an ordered <ol>.
Keep the current page as text, not a link, and mark it with aria-current="page".
The separator (›) is decorative, so hide it with aria-hidden.
